title.justification: The paper's title is clearly mentioned in the abstract and introduction sections.

extractions.description: The paper introduces a method for topological visual navigation that improves upon existing learning-based approaches. It proposes a sampling-based graph building method that results in sparser yet more efficient graphs for navigation tasks. The approach also includes graph maintenance strategies to refine navigational paths over time, allowing for improved performance in real-world environments when combined with minimal real-world data for fine-tuning. The method emphasizes using RGB-D images for constructing and maintaining navigation graphs.

primary_category.justification: The paper focuses on robotic navigation using visual data and does not directly relate to eco-responsible AI categories such as Climate Change Mitigation, Climate Change Adaptation, or others listed.
primary_category.quote: Nevertheless, spurious or missing edges in the topological graph often lead to navigation failure. In this work, we propose a sampling-based graph building method, which results in sparser graphs yet with higher navigation performance compared to baseline methods.

primary_sub_category.justification: The core focus of the paper on visual navigation does not align with any of the sub-categories listed for eco-responsible AI. The methodology is general and does not target specific environmental or climatic challenges.
primary_sub_category.quote: Unlike controllers that learn from fixed training environments, we show that our model can be fine-tuned using only a small number of collected trajectory images from a real-world environment where the agent is deployed.

new_primary_category.quote: We demonstrate successful navigation after fine-tuning on real-world environments, and notably show significant navigation improvements over time by applying our lifelong graph maintenance strategies.
